one_star_reviews.text:
Moved my grandfather into a care home and set up mail forwarding whilst he was away from the property.

E&M billed my grandfather during this time and obviously he wasn't at the address. The mail should have been forwarded but wasn't for whatever reason. Perhaps the letter was hand delivered?

We went to visit the property to freshen it up for sale and noticed a stack of mail.

From the timeline of events they billed him at the beginning of April and by mid May had already started court proceedings.

The property is a retirement block of flats so most of the residents are elderly.

What on earth are you doing escalating to court in the space of 6 weeks?? This is so devoid of empathy. There are numerous reasons why somebody in a retirement home is a few weeks behind paying a bill.

Of course we rang up to explain the situation - I could supply the care contract, the mail forwarding invoice and the sales listing for the flat to support my story. The person on the other end of the phone however refused to speak to us due to GDPR. Wouldn't even tell us what the bill was for which wasn't fully clear from the numerous letters we had received. Wouldn't even let us pay.

Unfortunately my grand father has dementia and we are in the process of sorting out power of attorney.

How unfortunate that my first and only experience with this company is one of such ruthlessness and cruelty.

Better hope your family stays healthy otherwise you might find they're on the other end of a court case within 6 weeks with a bill that has quintupled.

I visited Riverside Dental for a gum-related issue after seeing on Google that they offer direct dental hygiene appointments. However, for new patients, this is apparently not possible , something that was not clearly explained during booking and am expected to read all documents online before calling to book an appointment.

Their solicitor, Richard, visitied me while being detained in a Psychiatric Ward upon appealing my section. While going over my case, he pressurised me with aggressive questioning, claiming it would "prepare me for the hearing" and consequently failed to represent me properly during my CTO appeal upon discharge. He failed to read a crucial document provided by a family member written to the panel in support of my appeal, and while I attempted to respond to comments misrepresenting me, dismissed my defense as though he was acting in the interests of the panel and not myself.
After other participants finished giving evidence, he addressed me with a question. It was; why do you think you have been admitted to hospital as many times as you have? I was shocked that he was deliberately attempting to discredit me in view of the panel, and I couldn't think of an answer quickly enough. It was deeply unpleasant.
Solicitors should, according to law, always act in the best interests of the client, not just bend to norms that exist to prop up false notions of people's mental health.
I maintain that I do not suffer from any mental health issue and never have done. I refuse any psychotropic drugs and assert that I simply ended up in a cycle within a system that renders individuals dependant rather than empowered.
My assertion that I am normal unsettled Richard, and he failed to represent me when faced with members of the panel who subscribed to afforementioned long-held beliefs to do with mental health.

Poor aftercare and lack of accountability
From the very beginning, my experience with Amax has been disappointing. After signing the agreement, they attempted to change the payment terms, claiming a paperwork error. Then I had to chase for days before receiving a visit after paid my deposit.

Following installation, no user manual or guidance was provided.

When a fault developed with the panic alarm — the central unit continued flashing and could not be reset — I contacted Amax for support under their warranty. I received no response for four days. After following up, I was advised that the system was “not under maintenance” and directed to a generic YouTube video, before being told to contact the concierge team — who had already confirmed the issue was outside their remit.

As a customer who paid £1,080 for this installation, I expected basic aftercare. Instead I was redirected in circles with a “don’t bother me again” email, despite their own clause clearly stated that “ for a period of 12 months from the completion of the Installation Works it shall use reasonable endeavours to rectify any defect in the System following notification of the fault by the Customer.”

When we arrived, the place was clearly understaffed and overwhelmed. They had about 5 cars waiting to be dried or vacuumed and had formed two lanes of cars on the hand wash side. In hindsight I should have left but as we were there and in no rush we decided to wait patiently for our turn. Then as we got to the front after the initial wash awaiting a rinse without warning, the man in charge, who we later discovered was the 'boss', started gesturing manically to move forward at the same time screaming and swearing at me to get off my phone. I hadn't been on my phone at all,and  was trying to manoeuvre the car being mindful of the other car adjacent to me and with sud coated windscreen. My mum, already shaken from the hospital, became visibly upset and was not taking his disrespect.
When he was walking past her she opened her door slightly and calmly tried to address his unwarranted rudeness. Instead of apologising, he doubled down, denied swearing, and accused us of making it up. He then threatened to soak the inside of the car if we didn't drop it, and tried to slam her passenger door. He then opened the front passenger door and menacingly demanded that we leave the car wash as he did not need our business and then proceeded to slam the door so hard the window rattled violently, and repeatedly screamed and violently gestured for us  to leave and never come back.

I was absolutely furious, but with my vulnerable mum in the car and a challenging morning behind us, I kept my cool I wasn't about to give him any more of our energy or put her at further risk.

No customer should ever be treated like this especially not with a distressed elderly passenger in the vehicle. The way this man behaved was intimidating and completely unprofessional. I would strongly advise others to avoid this place. No one should have to put up with that level of aggression at a car wash.

I am writing this review to express my profound disappointment and frustration with the appalling level of service—or lack thereof—provided by this shop.

In early February, I purchased the Our Lady of Walsingham mug. It is now late April, and the item has never been received. Over the past nearly three months, I have attempted to resolve this through numerous follow-up emails, only to be met with "Matthew," whose professional conduct has been utterly irresponsible.

Initially, I chose to be patient and understanding. Matthew informed me that he only works two days a week, and I respected that timeframe. However, it is clear now that my kindness was taken for granted. For weeks, I was fed excuses about "checking with Royal Mail," yet no follow-up ever materialized. After months of these delays, Matthew promised to send a replacement mug. That never happened. When I finally reached my limit and requested a full refund, communication ceased entirely. I have been effectively ghosted.

This is not my first negative experience with this particular establishment. In 2017, while living in the UK, I ordered a statue of Our Lady of Walsingham from this store, only for it to arrive with the face broken off. I ended up having to glue the statue back together myself. At the time, I gave the benefit of the doubt, but this latest saga proves a systemic lack of quality control and accountability.

For a business that profits from the sale of Christian products, this behavior is particularly egregious. There is a complete absence of the integrity and ethical standards one would expect from a Christian retailer. Instead, there is a blatant disregard for statutory obligations and basic consumer rights.
Furthermore, I am left with the distinct and troubling impression that I am being treated this way because I am an international customer with a non-Caucasian last name. It appears Matthew believes he can ignore his responsibilities and disappear without consequence, assuming that a non-white customer abroad has no recourse and will simply "go away."

You have broken my trust and kept my money without delivering the goods. This is not just poor customer service; it is a total failure of professional and moral character. I strongly advise others—especially those ordering from outside the UK—to take their business elsewhere.

I am still demanding a full refund immediately.

I am currently unable to use my car due to an error caused by Halfords Great Yarmouth. I booked an MOT and service via the Internet, easy enough. My car failed on a couple of bits (suspension related) which I was willing to let them fix. They then stated that one part (front suspension) they could not fix because they either didn't have the resources to do so or they just didn't have the allocated time to do it, they suggested that I should take it to an independent garage because they can do the job better and cheaper! This meant I had to drive my car away to a different garage without an MOT to have it fixed elsewhere. (They had apparently fixed both rear springs for me though) When I had driven my car to it's destination it was apparent that there was something very wrong with my rear suspension. One side is at least 2 inches higher than the other and I have been advised not to drive it. After contacting them, they stated that I should take it back to them (even though it's not driveable) and they would take a look. After explaining that I couldn't drive it, their resolution was for me to pay for a transporter to deliver it to them! I am having to walk 45 minutes each way to work and my car will be stuck undriveable until this is resolved. I have complained to their head office but apparently it's not important enough to deal with quickly so I have around 7 days until they deal with it.

Also found out that while attempting to fix the front suspension, some of the bolts have been rounded off by the mechanic. They deny even touching the bolts although looking at them, it's obvious it's been rounded off by them as they have had the soot/grease taken off them by the sockets they use.

Updated. The car is now fixed and fully tested.

Once we had been accepted, I brought our identification in as asked to within the 48 hour window. That evening I received a rude call stating that we were going to lose our property as we hadn’t given our ID in. These were just two occasions of poor communication from WHB. Before moving in, our contracts were incorrectly filled in by WHB at least three times which made it a pain for the landlord having to sign it many times. I booked an appointment at Superdrug Pharmacy St Stephen for a yellow fever vaccination, which is required for travel to certain African countries. I paid £25 for the appointment, expecting a straightforward process.

Unfortunately, my experience was very disappointing. From the moment I entered the room, the nurse was rude and dismissive. While I understand that questions are necessary, I was asked an excessive number in an unprofessional manner. I clearly explained that I needed the vaccination to support my eVisa application for South Africa, and that my travel agency had advised me to get it. Despite this, she repeatedly argued that I did not need the vaccine.

To clarify, I even contacted a doctor during the appointment, who confirmed that it would be advisable to take the vaccination. Despite this professional opinion, the nurse still refused to administer it.

The situation became increasingly frustrating. I provided all the trip details she requested, yet she continued to be argumentative. Eventually, she ended the appointment without giving me the vaccine, stating that my time had run out and asking me to book another appointment an hour later. I then went to a different vaccination centre, where I received the vaccine within 10 minutes after filling out a simple form—no issues at all.

Overall, this was a very poor experience. The nurse demonstrated a lack of communication skills, professionalism, and basic customer care. I would not recommend this service.

I recently visited Cambridge Wine Merchants with my partner after wanting to come for quite some time. We both enjoy wine and had high expectations given the reputation of this place, but unfortunately, the experience was very, very disappointing.

My partner ordered a red wine glass and I ordered an orange wine glass.

While preparing my orange wine, I watched a staff member finish one bottle by shaking out repeatedly the very last drops - including the visible sediment - directly into my glass. Orange wines can naturally contain sediment, but this should be handled with care (e.g. avoiding pouring the lees unless explained). This resulted in a cloudy and unpleasant glass, full of sediment, as seen on the photo.
Not only that, a new bottle was then open and added to the same glass, which compromises the integrity and consistency of the wine, as you are effectively mixing two different bottles (potentially with different levels of oxidation or character) in a single serve.

Another unfortunate, and really sad, red flag was that a metal measuring tool was used to prepare my wine - which it is not perfect, but I will not be completely against - BUT alarmingly, the same metal measuring tool was used repeatedly across different wines without being rinsed in between! This leads to cross-contamination, impacting the aroma and flavour profile of each wine - something that is quite surprising in a venue that presents itself as wine-focused.

Less important but worthy to refer, the snack offer was sadly really limited too. The place offers three crisp options as a snack, which initially seemed like a reasonable selection. However, when I visited, I ordered one of the flavours and it was confirmed at the time. Only after the wine was already on the table was I told it was no longer available, and that in fact only one of the three options remained - unfortunately not one that either of us liked, so we ended up not ordering anything.

At last, despite the points mentioned above, my 1-star review is, unfortunately, focused on the service. When paying, I politely explained my concerns and, for the first time in our lives, we declined to pay the optional service charge. I approached this constructively, hoping the feedback might be useful. However, the response I received was dismissive (“uh-huh, ok”), with no apology or acknowledgment. This lack of basic customer care was honestly the most disappointing part of the visit.

Overall, it wasn’t just about the wine itself, but the combination of poor attention to detail and lack of professionalism in handling feedback. It’s a shame, as this is a place we were genuinely excited to visit.

Food was okay, service was horrific. We went as a group of 7, for bottomless brunch. Manager was rude, and we were not served for the final 45 minutes. Would not recommend, and will not be returning.

I came to Middletons for a Bottomless Brunch with a group of friends to celebrate a joint birthday. Upon arrival we were greeted with a very polite man who I think was the manager, he showed us to our table and was very friendly. When we sat down there was only us and 3 other tables. As we were looking at the menu we saw two members of staff playing a game of rock paper scissors behind the bar, a young lad with blonde hair and a young brunette girl. The young lad lost and rolled his eyes before looking at our table to which the manager said to him just go over there and get on with it. From us seeing this, it was in fact very obvious that they were playing rock, paper, scissors to decide who would serve our table. We found this very rude and insulting considering we had only come in 5 minutes ago and were causing no trouble (we’re a very quite bunch, it’s not like we were being loud).

When the young lad came over to take our order he asked us what cocktails we wanted as part of our bottomless brunch. Before making our decision, he told us it would be easier for them if we all had the same as then he could bring us a jug of that cocktail to share. This was disappointing as some of us wanted to try different ones but we didn’t want to be difficult so we went along with the jugs for ease. When the jugs of cocktails came, they were filled half full with ice and tasted like 90% fruit juice, very little alcohol in it - if any! This didn’t seem very good value considering we were paying £34.95 per person for unlimited cocktails and a main meal.

Towards the end of our experience the brunette lady came over and gave us our bill. She reassured us there was no rush to pay but she’d leave it on our table. Ten minutes later, she came over and said we have to pay now because they have a big table coming in. This was very abrupt and out of the blue and when we looked around the restaurant was empty apart from 5 tables so couldn’t see the hurry. Nevertheless, we paid the bill. It wasn’t until we all paid our part separately that we realised we had been charged for 8 bottomless brunches instead of 7. We were on a table of 8, but there were only 7 of us and only 7 meals that had been put through, so i’m unsure how this happened. We bought it up with the brunette lady and she disappeared. Instead of coming back over herself or sending the manager over, a different young lad came over who was very helpful and refunded us the extra we had paid by mistake.

We told the young lad about our experience and how we were made to feel at the start and then being rushed out at the end. The young lad apologised but it was a shame that the manager didn’t come over. When this was happening, the original two servers that we had (who played rock, paper, scissors) were smirking and laughing behind the bar.

I must say, I do feel thoroughly disappointed. Whenever I am in Norwich with my partner or family, I always come to middletons for a meal and this is why I suggested to my friends to come here for a bottomless brunch. But after the experience we have had from the staff here and how we were made to feel, I won’t be coming back again for a normal lunch or bottomless brunch. For the price we paid, I expected to be drinking freshly shaken cocktails made by the bar staff not a pre-made jug they get out within seconds.

I placed an order with Dako on 28th April with delivery originally expected for 12th May. Despite this, I only received communication regarding a delay on 11th May, and that was only after I had already emailed them myself on 8th May chasing for an update.

I was initially told the wardrobe had not yet been produced and later given explanations blaming warehouse and Bank Holiday delays. However, it has since become clear that the wardrobe had apparently not even been ordered until the day before the original delivery date. This makes the explanations regarding delays extremely misleading.

What makes this even more frustrating is that the company has repeatedly attempted to blame almost an entire month of issues, delays, and lack of communication on a single Bank Holiday that took place after the original order date. A one day Bank Holiday does not reasonably explain weeks of silence, failure to provide updates, failure to arrange proper customer contact, or the complete mishandling of an order.

Throughout the entire process, communication and customer service have been extremely poor. I requested direct phone contact more than four times yet was continually ignored, with all communication limited to delayed email responses. I was also unable to get through to the company properly by phone myself.

After almost a month of waiting, Dako then attempt to deliver a completely different wardrobe to the one I actually ordered, despite the replacement item being significantly cheaper than the wardrobe I originally paid for by almost £100.

At this point, I am now almost one month on from placing my order and still do not have the correct wardrobe I originally purchased.

For a company taking full payment upfront for large furniture orders, this entire experience has been unacceptable. The issue is no longer simply delays. It is the lack of transparency, misleading information, poor communication, failure to properly manage the order, and ultimately delivering the wrong product altogether.

Very disappointing experience and not a level of service I would expect from a legitimate furniture company.

I placed an order with Dako on 28th April with delivery originally expected for 12th May. Despite this, I only received communication regarding a delay on 11th May, and that was only after I had already emailed them myself on 8th May chasing for an update.

I was initially told the wardrobe had not yet been produced and later given explanations blaming warehouse and Bank Holiday delays. However, it has since become clear that the wardrobe had apparently not even been ordered until the day before the original delivery date. This makes the explanations regarding delays extremely misleading.

What makes this even more frustrating is that the company has repeatedly attempted to blame almost an entire month of issues, delays, and lack of communication on a single Bank Holiday that took place after the original order date. A one day Bank Holiday does not reasonably explain weeks of silence, failure to provide updates, failure to arrange proper customer contact, or the complete mishandling of an order.

Throughout the entire process, communication and customer service have been extremely poor. I requested direct phone contact more than four times yet was continually ignored, with all communication limited to delayed email responses. I was also unable to get through to the company properly by phone myself.

After almost a month of waiting, Dako then attempt to deliver a completely different wardrobe to the one I actually ordered, despite the replacement item being significantly cheaper than the wardrobe I originally paid for by almost £100.

At this point, I am now almost one month on from placing my order and still do not have the correct wardrobe I originally purchased.

For a company taking full payment upfront for large furniture orders, this entire experience has been unacceptable. The issue is no longer simply delays. It is the lack of transparency, misleading information, poor communication, failure to properly manage the order, and ultimately delivering the wrong product altogether.

Very disappointing experience and not a level of service I would expect from a legitimate furniture company.

Up until recently I would have given this company a good rating but due to a severe lack of communication regarding the new Renter’s Rights Act I have now lost a huge amount of money thanks to Progressive Lets.

I’m in the process of moving home and had to discover on May 1st, the day the act took effect, that this company now requires a 2 month notice period when moving  even though I planned to move at the end of the month. Not even 2 weeks prior to writing this I received an email reminding me to remember to “hand in my 1 month notice when i’m ready” with no mention of this upcoming and very costly change which has now left me in a £800+ hole as i’m being forced to pay an extra month for an empty flat.

I tried to explain my situation and ask for a shorter 1-month notice period (which official government documentation states may be agreed upon) but was met with rude and blunt emails stating that Progressive Lets has ticked their legal box by sending a PDF in March which briefly mentions this change. Since then there has been no communications regarding this major change to their Ts & Cs.

I had foolishly hoped this company was different and would work with me to work out a plan that wouldn’t ruin my life but don’t be fooled, you’re still just a number on a spreadsheet to these people.

Please avoid this company at all costs if you’re expecting to find people who have your best interests as a tenant at heart. I really hope nobody has to go through this frustrating and heartbreaking experience in the future and I hope this company gets a lot better at notifying its tenants of major changes which could cost them to lose hundreds of pounds.

UPDATE: Instead of trying to find a resolution I get a heartless copy and paste response ignoring most of the points I made and reaffirming my stance on this company doing the bare minimum. Also apparently losing hundreds of pounds is now just deemed “inconvenient”. Avoid at all costs for your own sake if you’re reading this. Wouldn’t recommend to my worst enemy.

I visited this establishment on Sunday 10th May, and as a diagnosed Coeliac I am absolutely appalled by the sheer lack of empathy and negligence regarding cross-contamination.

Upon entering, I noticed a chocolate cake sitting uncovered in a corner next to a stack of brownies, with zero labeling. There was, however, a GF label next to a domed cake with white frosting. Naturally, I assumed the domed cake was the gluten-free option. I ordered the ‘gluten-free chocolate cake’ from the menu. When it arrived, it had a flake on the side, making me instantly suspicious. I asked the server if it was actually gluten-free and she had absolutely no idea and had to ask someone else. She then returned and shrugged it off, saying, "It must be, as that's the only one we have”, which in itself is not very assuring, but I trusted the server. As it turns out, the domed cake with the actual GF label next to it was a carrot cake.

Because the menu boasts numerous GF items, I trusted that the staff would be properly trained on allergen safety, especially working in a ‘customer service’ based establishment. I unknowingly ate half of the completely uncovered chocolate cake that had been sitting exposed to cross-contamination for the entire time we were there, (around 1.5 hours).

Predictably, within a couple of hours, I was hit with severe nausea and spent hours vomiting. I am a diagnosed Coeliac and know exactly what it feels like to be glutened, and this was a direct result of their carelessness.

To make matters worse, my husband called the following day to complain. He spoke to a manager (who wasn't the manager working on the Sunday we visited) who unhelpfully said that "the GF cakes were not covered for the entirety of our stay." (I'm not sure how she knew this as she was not on shift). When my husband protested and told her it was left completely bare for hours, the manager offered absolutely zero apology, which you would assume would be the very least, or even my money back.

If you are a Coeliac, avoid this place like the plague. They talk a big game on their menu, but their actual handling standards are nonexistent, and their customer service when they make someone violently ill is defensive, unsupportive and very unprofessional. I will never return.

I’ve been going to Indigo for years, mostly for tattoos, and I’ve always had really positive experiences with the staff. That’s why this visit was so disappointing.

I went in simply to ask about buying a floating navel bar for my belly button piercing. I was told I might need to wait for Candice, who I hadn’t seen before, but that was absolutely fine. However, the interaction that followed left me feeling quite uncomfortable.

After briefly looking at my piercing—in front of other staff and customers—she said, “that is rejecting” in a very blunt and dismissive tone. The way it was said felt rude and lacked any sensitivity, especially considering it’s something quite personal. She came across as standoffish and not particularly willing to help or explain things in a reassuring or professional way.

When I tried to explain my past experiences with this piercing, she was very dismissive and cut me off, saying, “well you don’t believe me, I’ve been doing this for 20 years, I know a rejecting piercing when I see one, I’ll just give you a bar,” before abruptly walking off. The whole interaction felt rushed, uncomfortable, and honestly quite unprofessional.

I completely respect professional advice and would have been open to hearing her opinion if it had been delivered in a more respectful and considerate way. The issue wasn’t what she said, but how she said it. When you’re dealing with customers and their bodies, tone and approach really matter—otherwise it can come across as unkind and make people feel self-conscious.

It’s a real shame because I’ve always had great experiences here and will likely still return for tattoos. However, this experience has definitely put me off returning for piercings, particularly if I were to be seen by the same staff member again. one_star_reviews.text:
As landlords, we were very disappointed with our experience using MAC Estates as our letting agents over the past couple of years.

When our tenants vacated the property, we expected the outgoing inspection to be carried out thoroughly and professionally. The report itself was over 160 pages long and included photographs of very minor marks, such as scuffs on radiators, however the significant damage to the skirting boards was not identified or highlighted anywhere in the report. From the photographs, the damage appears clearly visible and should reasonably have been picked up during the inspection.

As this damage was not included in the outgoing report, the tenants’ deposit was returned and we have been left covering the repair costs ourselves. We were disappointed that no responsibility was acknowledged for this oversight and we did not feel supported in resolving the issue.

In addition, our tenants had signed a pet declaration agreement which stated that the carpets would be cleaned and a flea treatment carried out at the end of the tenancy. However, as shown in the photographs, the carpets were not left in an acceptable condition. Although we were eventually able to claim £250 from the tenant towards a professional carpet clean, this only happened because we raised the issue ourselves. It did not feel as though these agreements were proactively checked or enforced by the letting agents during the checkout process.

Communication was also frustrating at times. Although the tenants reportedly provided 30 days’ notice, we were only informed around 20 days before they were due to leave. We were advised this was due to staff annual leave and an out-of-office notification not being activated, which unfortunately left us with less notice than expected.

This was our first experience renting out our home as young landlords, so we relied heavily on our letting agents to guide and support us through the process. Unfortunately, our experience did not give us the confidence or reassurance we had hoped for.

We hope this feedback is taken constructively and helps improve communication, accountability, and attention to detail for future landlords.

I was admitted via A&E to the gynaecology ward with severe bleeding and remained in hospital for five days without being gynaecologically examined by a doctor or consultant. I was discharged with a diagnosis of a simple haemorrhagic ovarian cyst and reassured that it would resolve on its own. I was also told that leaving blood in the pelvis was beneficial for my iron levels.

Unfortunately, due to a lack of appropriate investigation, diagnosis, and care, I later developed serious complications and was diagnosed with Endometriosis three months later. Blood that was left in my pelvis contributed to inflammation, lesion activity, and adhesion formation. Since then, I have been left with chronic, debilitating pelvic pain, endometrial cysts, and adhesions. This has had a lasting and significant impact on my health and quality of life.

There is no ward rounds involving patients in their care. I was not informed that my bleeding was significant, nor was I prescribed any medication upon discharge or offered a follow-up appointment. After weeks of pain and suffering I had to make formal complaint just to be seen for proper examination. As a result of this experience, I have lost trust in the medical profession.

This was my third visit to the pub, and sadly it turned what should have been a special birthday celebration into a very disappointing experience.

On my first visit, things didn’t go to plan, but the staff were apologetic and provided a voucher for a return visit. The second time was excellent — the food was lovely, and the atmosphere was relaxed — which gave me the confidence to book my birthday meal here for a larger group, with three weeks’ notice.

In the lead-up to the booking, we contacted the pub on four separate occasions to arrange a pre-order, as communication was unclear and we often had to chase for responses. The night before our booking, we were finally contacted to confirm the pre-order, which we promptly sent via email.

We arrived at 3:00pm for our 3:30pm table, expecting that, having pre-ordered, everything would run smoothly so we could enjoy the live band starting around 4:00–4:30pm. However, upon arrival, we were informed that our pre-order had not been received and our meals would need to be prepared from scratch. While this was frustrating, we were understanding and agreed to proceed.

Unfortunately, we then waited over an hour and a half for our food, with no communication or apology from staff during this time. The pub had become very busy, the band had started, and we were left feeling increasingly uncomfortable and overlooked. I eventually had to ask where our meals were.

When the food did arrive, the starters were brought out at the same time as the mains, and much of it was not particularly hot. I cannot fault the quality of the food itself, but the service was extremely poor throughout.

We chose to move outside to eat and requested to speak with the manager. It took some time for him to come over, and by that point I was extremely upset. Other customers even approached us, commenting on how shocked they were by the service we had received.

The manager offered complimentary desserts for the children and said he would return to discuss the bill, but he never came back. The children’s desserts took a further 40 minutes to arrive. When we asked for the bill, this also took another 40 minutes.

To add to our frustration, a 5% service charge had been included, and the “complimentary” desserts were still listed at £26 (despite being valued at £14). We again asked to speak with the manager, but he did not come. When we raised concerns, we were met with rudeness from staff, including eye-rolling from the waitress.

The situation escalated into an argument, during which the manager stated that he was “not profiting” from our visit and ultimately banned us from the pub. This was both shocking and upsetting, particularly given the circumstances.

Although a portion of the bill was eventually removed, it felt begrudging and did not reflect the level of service we received. Overall, the experience was extremely disappointing and completely overshadowed what should have been an enjoyable birthday celebration.

It’s particularly disappointing because the pub itself is beautiful and the live band was fantastic. With better organisation and communication, this could have been a wonderful experience. Unfortunately, it feels like the team are not equipped to handle busy periods, and something in their processes is clearly not working as it should.

Extremely poor service and dangerous standards. If I could give no stars I would!

I had a very serious incident after having an MOT here. The bonnet was not secured properly by the technician and flew open at speed with my young daughter in the car, causing significant damage.

Despite this being a life threatening incident, I was incredibly reasonable. I told them human errors happen and I just wanted them to put it right. They accepted full liability and paid over £1k for all the parts and repairs.

When I collected the car, I checked the front and was happy with the work. Due to it pouring with rain, I didn't check everything else. We noticed a plastic part was missing when we got in the car which the technician agreed to order. However, when we got home we found further damage.

They returned my car with chemical residue all over my diamond cut alloy wheels which has caused permanent damage. I messaged them immediately on Facebook as they had closed.

On the Monday I took the car back to show them and was met by the Director. This is where everything changed completely.

He completely changed his story and denied liability for the accident. He either tried to gaslight me or made a serious slip-up, suddenly claiming the latch had been "faulty".

I obviously raised the serious question of: If the latch was faulty, why did it NOT fail the MOT? He ignored this completely.

Either way they are liable - whether it wasn't latched or it was faulty.

He then denied liability for everything and tried to claim the bright yellow residue on my wheel was "mud", despite it clearly causing permanent damage to two of my alloys. There was also black oily residue on another alloy which he managed to partially clean off. I have time-stamped photos proving the condition of my alloys before they went in, showing the severe damage they caused.

When I requested paperwork and invoices, he actually told me I didn't need them.

Instead of apologising, he accused me of trying to "pull the wool over his eyes" and get more than I was entitled to. I became very upset and started crying. I was left completely distraught over what was originally a £55 MOT.

It is so upsetting after how reasonable I was. I trusted them, I defended them, and this is how they treated me.

Continued review… (part 2)

I sent a polite email explaining I am legally entitled to these documents and warning I would report them to the DVSA if the alloys weren't put right. He replied saying he values his customers - which is hard to believe after making me cry, damaging my car twice, and denying all responsibility despite previously paying over £1k in damages.

He did eventually send some documents, but crucially there was no record of any work being done to the latch, despite him claiming that was the fault. I have asked for the complete documentation I am legally entitled to, but they have failed to provide it and are now ignoring all communication.

In his email he offered to restore all 4 alloys, but due to the total breakdown of trust and the way I have been treated, I told him I do not consent to Saracens touching my car again. I stated I would obtain two quotes from independent specialists for them to pay, which I am entitled to under the Consumer Rights Act. This has also been ignored.

This will be the first and last time I ever use this garage. I gave them until April 6th to make this right, but they have chosen silence.

If they do not respond and rectify this, I will be reporting them to the DVSA and proceeding with a claim for repairs, vehicle devaluation, my £55 MOT fee back, and emotional distress via Small Claims Court.

I am also posting this warning to the 17,000 members of the Fakenham Facebook page if I don’t get a response back this week.

They cannot be trusted to carry out work correctly, be honest with customers, or take responsibility when things go wrong. I would not recommend them to anyone - if this review is still up it means they never rectified my alloys off their own back.

one_star_reviews.text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but my experience with Mario Removals was extremely disappointing.

During our move, their team dismantled and reassembled a wooden playground. What we were left with was unsafe and poorly put together — loose screws, missing fittings, and parts not properly secured.

To this day, the structure still does not stand in a stable condition, the way it used to. Until I can afford to have a professional come in to properly fix what was done, my kids are effectively deprived of something they should be able to enjoy safely but Mario removals clearly have no care or consideration.

When I raised the issue, they initially refused to take responsibility. Instead, they suggested the problems were due to how the playing fort had originally been built, uneven ground, or weather-related wear — none of which were accurate. These explanations were given despite evidence showing the structure was previously stable and correctly assembled.

It was only after I pushed back firmly and raised the possibility of legal action that any acknowledgment of poor workmanship was made. Even then, no meaningful resolution was offered. I was still charged the full amount, with no compensation despite what happened.

What was most frustrating was not just the mistake itself, but the lack of accountability and professionalism in handling the complaint. There was no initial apology, and the response felt dismissive rather than supportive.

Moving house is already stressful — customers should be able to trust that their belongings will be handled with care and that any issues will be addressed properly. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I would not recommend this company.

The Easter egg hunt was another let down—we were given a sheet to complete and told there would be a prize, but this turned out to be a small 10p pack of Haribo. Overall, it was not good value for money and didn’t meet expectations for what should have been a special family experience. Do not be mislead by the social media influencers.

We hired Katie to decorate our entire home during a major renovation. This was by far the worst experience we’ve had with any tradesperson.

Her initial quote after the survey was imprecise and unclear; we asked for clarification, which she gave verbally, and we proceeded in good faith also on the basis of her being recommended by friends. That trust was clearly misplaced.
She went in and out our property as she pleased (while the house was inhabited) as we provided her with the key in good faith, however we would have appreciated clear communication on her presence in the house out of respect.

The job was quoted at 2–3 weeks for a four-bedroom house. After over two months, it still wasn’t finished. She regularly started late, left early, and often didn’t show up at all without notice, sometimes disappearing for days with no communication. In fairness, we asked her not to be at the property for a total of no more than 7 days over the course of 2 months due to clashing with other works, and she had at times to work around other tradesmen, however we cannot accept this to be the reason for her to fail delivering the project.

We faced repeated, last-minute instalment payment demands with personal excuses (food; rent; entertainment) and pressure to pay immediately — completely unprofessional also because this type of payment was never agreed upfront.

Despite multiple discussions and a clear deadline, she failed to complete the work. One room was left unfinished and many areas were poorly done including panelling, staircase and ceilings, forcing me to step in to fix during late nights — especially as we had to move in based on her original timeline.

After moving in, she reluctantly returned to fix some issues, but the quality remained poor and in some cases made things worse. It took repeated effort to get her back.

We seriously question her understanding of basic decorating techniques (e.g. cutting in, correct use of matt vs gloss, painting panels). The number of beginner mistakes means we do not consider her a professional decorator.

Don’t be misled by low pricing — you’ll likely pay more to fix the work or hire a real professional.

Overall, a stressful and disappointing experience, we recommend looking elsewhere. Lots of local professional decorators out there

I visited the Holt Clearance Shop today with the intention of purchasing a cardigan. I asked a member of staff a lady with short grey hair, likely in her late 60s, if they had any in stock.

Her response was, “Is it for you?” followed by looking me up and down. When I confirmed it was, she replied, “Then no, not in your size.”

I was completely taken aback by this interaction. The comment felt unnecessary, inappropriate, and unkind.

To be clear, I am in lifelong recovery from an eating disorder. Had I been in a more vulnerable place, this experience could have had a serious impact on my wellbeing.

I would strongly encourage the store owner to address this matter whether through appropriate disciplinary action or, at the very least, additional customer service training. No customer should be made to feel judged or diminished in this way.

As it stands, I will not be returning, and I will be sharing this experience within the local community.

one_star_reviews.text:
In the first week of March I ordered a Jane Austen themed bag from this shop online to give to my friend as a gift. I got an email after ordering from Cara at the shop to let me know that the item was out of stock but should be back within a number of weeks, or alternatively they had the same bag available in a different colour. I responded advising that I needed the bag by the 10th April for a birthday gift so asked if the colour I ordered would be available by then and, if not, I would be happy with the alternative colour option; Cara responded that if they heard that the bag in the colour I had ordered would not be available in time then they will contact me and offer to send the navy one out instead; I agreed to this and at this time felt that I was receiving good customer service. Unfortunately, after this the shop's communication and care ceased and I had to chase. On 31/03, I had had no contact from the shop so emailed Cara asking where things are up to with the bags, after no response I emailed again and copied in the main shop email on 02/04. As 03/04 - 06/04 was a bank holiday weekend I was conscious of this impacting delivery times. I live in Manchester but by a lucky(?) coincidence I happened to be in Norwich over the bank holiday weekend so I was able to go to the shop to pick up the bag, as at this point it was unlikely to be delivered in time. I called the shop on 03/04 as had no response to the emails and was advised by Moss that the bag I ordered was not available but he would send me photos of the bags that were available. Unfortunately, I felt that I had no choice but to accept a bag that was not what we had ordered as I had no time to ensure that the original Jane Austen bag would be delivered if ordered from elsewhere, so I ended up with a Shakespeare themed one instead. Moss was not empathetic or understanding of my situation - he blamed the company that makes the bags and even blamed the war in Iran. I understand that it must be frustrating for the shop if they are not receiving their stock, however my issue was with their lack of communication and customer service which Moss would not accept. I asked if they could offer me anything due to my dissatisfaction with their lack of customer service; I spotted a Jane Austen purse in the shop so asked if they would consider letting us have this to gift to my friend and he refused, and instead gave me a much cheaper purse that is of no use to me or my friend - when he gave me this purse he said "are you happy now?".
I would also like to add that the money for the original bag we had ordered was taken as soon as the order was placed, despite them not having this in stock - I would suggest that they don't list out of stock items on their website as available to buy.
If I didn't happen to be in Norwich that weekend, or if I had not chased contact with the shop I believe they would have kept my money and I would have never received a product (or at least not in time to gift to my friend).

BE AWARE - AVOID WHITE X5 ‘GY17 BFA’!!
I travelled from Northern Ireland, at great expense, to buy a BMW X5 (GY17 BFA) from this garage. There were some issues with the car that I wanted to be put right before coming to buy the car; they requested a further £300 on top of their standard £199 holding deposit to do so. I agreed with the caveat that I would expect it to be be refunded in the event that the car is not as expected - I clarified this in writing.

Upon arrival the car was, cosmetically, ok. When I took the car for a test drive there was a major and obvious power delivery issue that I suspected was turbo related. When I returned to the garage it took 30 seconds of googling to find that this is a known issue with this specific model relating to vacuum lines and control- and that it was an intermittent fault that will reset when the vehicle is turned off but will reoccur.

The manager refused to believe this and refused to refund the additional £300 deposit.

I would highly recommend avoiding this garage. The manager, Lee, is particularly unpleasant.

UPDATE - car has now been relisted on Autotrader. It is my opinion, that no fault finding has been undertaken and that this dealership is untrustworthy.

The salesman was actually pretty helpful. However, after we'd agreed to go ahead that's when the problems started to arise.

Surveyor appointment booking was fine, turned up on time. However, they made a mistake. It took weeks for Anglian to get back to me after repeated attempts to get them to confirm the designs and notes they'd written were incorrect and needed updating.

Installation date was organised easily enough but I was already a little apprehensive at this point and just hoped that there were no further issues with the installation etc as I was not hopeful that this company would actually resolve anything if there was.

Installation day came. The scaffolders Anglian had arranged (Next Level Scaffolding East Ltd.) didn't turn up on the day before when they should have. Darren phoned to say the team were still coming and would be doing overtime and would arrive at around 5pm - nothing.
They arrived about 7:30am the following day, the same day that Anglian were supposed to install our new roof-trim, gutters and facia. The fitters themselves turned up around 8am, noticed the scaffolding wasn't up and so said they'd be back the next day - fine.

Scaffolding didn't quite get fully complete on the original install day and so they had to finish off the following day whilst the fitters were here.

All was ok.

The fitters completed their work on the 8th May. All looked ok. They tidied up a little but left rubbish in gutters and on our conservatory roof. They could have done a better job there.

I was told scaffolding would be removed on the following Monday (11th May).

11th May comes round. No sign of scaffolders.
It wasn't until that Friday (15th May) that I checked the inspection tag they left on the scaffolding to find the phone number and details of the scaffolding company to ask them what was going on. I spoke to Anglian who said they would chase this but heard no response.
Darren at Next Level Scaffolding East Ltd. said that they would be over on the Wednesday morning to remove the scaffolding.
Bear in mind, the scaffolding had been up for 10 consecutive days at this point without inspection - which is illegal.
Wednesday arrives. The scaffolders turn up at around 12:40pm. They start removing the scaffolding without communication. At around 3pm I noticed they had started leaving the scaffolding in piles on our front garden. I asked them whether this was going to be taken away today and they said they were leaving it there to take back the following morning.
This was completely unacceptable. Not only had they abused using my property as a storage area for over 1 week (illegally) they then took it upon themselves to find a part of my garden to leave their materials for the night. Why they didn't bring enough trucks to take the scaffolding away in the first place is beyond me. They were confrontational and Darren, the owner of the company, unprofessional. Darren even went as far as suggested they put it back up again if leaving it in pieces on the garden wasn't acceptable - to say the least his team shot that idea down pretty quickly! It was laughable...
It was clear they were not going to take it away that day and so I agreed to let them leave it there for one night (ONLY).
They should be back tomorrow to collect it all but we'll see if they turn up.
All along, I have kept Anglian in the loop but hear NOTHING. No support. Even though they are technically liable as the scaffolding contract was arranged by them.

To make matters worse, now that the scaffolding was removed and we could see out of our windows onto our conservatory roof, we have found that a block of wood has fallen from the scaffolding and pieced the roof causing a whole around the size of a penny.
I have contacted Anglian about this but expect a long, hard fight to get them to even acknowledge this and perform a repair/replacement of the roof panel...

PLEASE TAKE HEED OF THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS ON HERE!
To save likely stress and additional expense avoid this company at all costs!
Similarly avoid Next Level Scaffolding East (based in Norwich)!

AVOID!
We had to use WGA swaffham as executors for my mother's will as they are who she chose.
We had to wait THREE weeks just to get an initial meeting with the solicitor who was to take on the work. She then went on maternity leave and work was handed over to another more senior person who charged more per hour if we had needed her to take on anything extra....not acceptable that we should have been expected to pay an inflated hourly rate in these circumstances!
This "senior" solicitor, we called "the silent solicitor", we just didn't hear from her unless we chased it up!
Once property was sold etc. she made an initial payment to us and kept back a sum to pay final bills once they were all in.  The sum held back was £1000s more than was ever going to be necessary to pay these final balances, no doubt WGA get interest payments for everyone's money they keep back!!  call me cynical!
The estate was not a complex one by any means, we disputed the final cost (which came in right at the top end of the original estimate.... funny that) as it seemed excessive.
We had to chase up (again) regarding the final release of funds to us, found they were waiting on the council for final council tax bill.  They chased this up and found there was nothing to pay, account closed but hadn't heard from the council to this effect.  How long would WGA have waited before contacting the council if we hadn't chased for it??
They refused to release any further funds (OUR MONEY) to us until we had "approved" their final bill. basically holding it for ransom.
Do yourself a favour, DO NOT USE this dreadful company. They fleece you, do as little as possible for the money and don't contact you to keep you updated.
Absolutely disgusted with their service.  No doubt I'll get the standard "sorry to hear this, contact our customer service director...... etc." which seems to be the reply to any bad reviews they receive.

I’m very disappointed with the aftercare from Anglia WoodBurner Centre.

They originally installed my stove in 2013, so I returned to them in July 2025 for servicing and replacement of the internal vermiculite brick set (cost well over £300). Unfortunately, after only around 20 uses, by December 2025 two of the bricks had already developed significant cracks. The roof brick in particular has failed structurally and begun to collapse downward, making the stove unusable.

There has been no impact or misuse, and the bricks were supplied as pre-cut components and installed by Anglia WoodBurner Centre.

I first raised the issue on 5 January 2026 and followed up multiple times (including 18 January and 29 January), as well as speaking to staff and the manager by phone in February. I was advised the issue would be escalated to the supplier and that I would receive an update, but I have received no meaningful response as of April 2026.  My formal complaint to them in March was also ignored.

This is particularly disappointing given I was a returning customer from their original installation.

I am not seeking anything unreasonable, simply replacement of the failed components so the stove can be used safely, but the lack of communication has been frustrating.

I hope this review encourages a response and helps others understand the level of after-sales support they can expect.

— the handling of this situation has become even more concerning.

I had a very disappointing and frustrating experience with Tax Resolute.

I signed a contract with Jesmin at a rate of £300 per hour after being introduced to her by my accountant. It was clearly agreed that my accountant would handle the accounting side, while Jesmin would liaise with HMRC.

However, after the contract was signed, she outsourced the work to someone else (Craig), who was charging her £200 per hour, while I was still billed £300 per hour. Throughout the case, Jesmin herself did not meaningfully contribute. I paid for her expertise, not for work to be passed on to someone else without transparency.

Because the contract was hourly-based, I believe the hours were significantly overstated. For example, even WhatsApp messages I sent that were never responded to were billed in 1-minute increments. This is completely unreasonable.

I requested a detailed timesheet in December 2024 and continued to chase it multiple times, but it was only provided in May 2025—by which point the total had already reached 95 hours. This made it impossible to properly monitor or challenge the billing as the work progressed.

I am disputing around 50 of those hours as they are clearly inflated and unsupported by evidence. In fact, they themselves admitted errors and removed 14 hours that they could not justify. Despite this, they continue to claim the remaining hours are substantiated, which I strongly disagree with. Even my accountant was shocked by the number of billable hours.

It appears that because Jesmin has already paid the outsourced worker, she is now attempting to pass those costs onto me without sufficient evidence. She has even tried to recover money from him, and when that failed, is now pursuing me instead.

To make matters worse, during the initial call before signing the contract, I was told the work would take approximately 50–60 hours. Yet the final bill nearly doubled that estimate at 95 hours.

Additionally, they have attempted to charge me for accounting work, which is completely unacceptable, as this was always meant to be handled by my accountant. This was clearly agreed in the initial meeting between myself, my accountant, Jesmin, and Craig.

My advice to others: NEVER agree to an hourly contract without strict oversight. If you do, insist on frequent and transparent timesheets throughout the engagement.

Overall, I feel misled, overcharged, and extremely dissatisfied with the service. Jesmin did not personally handle my case as expected, and the billing practices lack transparency and credibility.

Absolutely disgraceful treatment from East Suffolk Council.

I am a disabled woman living alone and I have spent months fighting with the council over repeated Council Tax errors that should have been resolved the first time evidence was submitted.

I repeatedly provided evidence for Single Person Discount and disability-related reductions, including medical evidence and disability documentation, yet the council continued issuing incorrect bills, ignoring submissions, failing to properly process forms already sent to them, and threatening recovery action for amounts that appear to be wrong because of THEIR repeated administrative failures.

At this point, I genuinely cannot understand how this level of incompetence is even possible.

The same mistakes have been repeated over and over and over again despite multiple contacts, multiple submissions of evidence, and repeated attempts to resolve matters properly. Every response takes an excessive amount of time, and when they finally do respond it is often with more incorrect information, more ignored evidence, and more failures.

The process has been utterly exhausting and has had a severe impact on both my physical and mental health. I have spent months under extreme stress trying to correct mistakes that should never have happened in the first place.

What concerns me most is how vulnerable and disabled residents are expected to navigate a system like this. I have spoken to other disabled people living alone who were completely unaware they may be entitled to reductions at all. Why is there not clearer guidance? Why are people having to fight this hard for support they are legally entitled to?

When a council repeatedly ignores evidence, repeatedly fails to process forms, repeatedly issues incorrect bills, and continues threatening enforcement action anyway, it raises extremely serious concerns about competence, accountability, and how vulnerable residents are being treated.

If this is happening to me after months of fighting, I dread to think how many other vulnerable people are quietly paying incorrect amounts simply because they do not have the health, knowledge, or energy to keep battling the council’s failures.

Completely unacceptable.

I have now formally raised an official complaint regarding the handling of this matter after months of repeated errors, ignored evidence, incorrect billing, and ongoing administrative failures by East Suffolk Council.

Given the sheer number of mistakes already made throughout this process, I have very little confidence that the complaint itself will even be handled competently, but at this stage I feel I have been left with no other option.

No vulnerable or disabled resident should have to spend months fighting the same repeated mistakes simply to have the correct reductions and entitlements properly applied.

I am very disappointed with the service at Manor Farm Medical Centre.

My issues started with a prescription for a full month of medication (28 tablets). However, I was only given 14 days’ supply and told that the remaining tablets were out of stock and would be provided within a few days at no extra cost. This was also written on the packaging, and I have proof of this.

After waiting, I was told the stock still had not arrived and that I would be contacted. I never received any update. When I returned because my medication was almost finished, I was eventually given tablets. However, I later discovered that a new prescription had been created without my knowledge or consent, and I was then asked to pay again.

Shortly after, I received a message warning that if I did not pay, I could face NHS penalties. This was very confusing, as I had already paid for the original prescription. I was then told that the dosage had been changed from 2.5 mg to 5 mg and that I could split the tablets, even though I never requested any change. The medication was initially dispensed through the GP practice dispensary.

When I raised these issues, I was repeatedly told different explanations, and there was no clear communication or accountability.

In relation to my urine tests, I was advised by a doctor that a repeat sample would be required after 4–6 weeks. However, when I returned within that timeframe, I was informed that the previous sample had been disposed of. I was not given a clear explanation as to why this occurred. I am also concerned that my second urine sample does not appear on the NHS App or in the system, despite being submitted.

In addition, I dealt with the reception manager Alis, who gave inconsistent explanations about missing records and system issues. I was told my information had been “missed due to volume in the system” and asked to provide another sample. Even after doing so, there was still no record available. I was also informed that a sample had been destroyed, which is extremely concerning given the lack of clear documentation.

I also had a phone call with Dr. Kalin, which I did not request. I had clearly asked to speak with a manager regarding administrative issues, not a doctor. During the call, I was told that if I was not satisfied with the practice, I could consider registering elsewhere. I found this response inappropriate, as my concern was about receiving fair and proper administrative handling, not personal preference.

Overall, communication throughout this process has been very poor. Emails are not properly answered, and it is extremely difficult to reach a manager directly. Requests to speak with management are redirected or ignored.

I want to make it clear that I remained respectful at all times. I did not use any abusive language. My frustration came from repeatedly feeling ignored, misinformed, and treated unfairly as a patient.

Overall, I feel that the handling of my case has been inconsistent and concerning, and at times has given the impression of a lack of willingness to properly address or resolve patient concerns. At times, it has felt as though raising concerns is discouraged rather than properly addressed.

I used to have a very positive opinion of this GP practice and have even left a five-star review in the past. However, based on my recent experience with Alis, Dr. Kalin, and the administration process, I am very disappointed and would not recommend this practice in its current state

From my perspective, this creates a contradiction: on one hand there is an expectation of support and engagement from others, but on the other hand there is no basic communication or acknowledgment in return. At the same time, the education programme appears to be used for marketing purposes.

This has been very disappointing for me, as I expected a more respectful and reciprocal human approach. It has affected my trust in the farm and my overall perception of it.

What is also striking is the human attitude here, and it makes me question how much trust can be placed in the future if this is the moral standard.

For me, it simply crossed a line, and it has completely shaken my trust in the farm and its products.

When we challenged it, as was our right, Lexadon relented. Advice to current tenants would be to catalogue everything, stand your ground and don't be afraid to raise disputes with TDS.

Renting in London can be hard enough as it is - Lexadon only make it ten times worse. AVOID!

Upon moving in there were multiple issues with our rental property that were agreed to be remediated before moving in, in addition to more issues once we had the keys including a water leak, broken fittings, etc.

Over email we were passed around and heard little contact. Most of the problems raised are still outstanding despite being told they were getting looked into, and we now struggle to hear a response from the team. Quite disappointing and put a damper on our move.

Our experience with Lexadon Property Group was wholly unacceptable and demonstrated a consistent pattern of negligence and disregard for tenant welfare.

Severe black mould was reported no fewer than 20 times over the course of the year. Rather than addressing the root cause, we were repeatedly told to “wipe it off with a towel,” and their only action was to paint over it. The situation escalated to the point where mould spread onto our clothes and shoes. A review of other tenant feedback indicates this is not an isolated incident, but a recurring issue across multiple properties they manage.

The bottom bedroom flooded on two separate occasions, resulting in the destruction of personal belongings. On both occasions, the issue was met with prolonged inaction and weeks of unresponsiveness, with no meaningful effort to resolve the damage or prevent recurrence.

Hygiene and maintenance standards were equally concerning. Slugs were entering the property through the shower, highlighting serious underlying issues with the condition of the building. Upon moving in, it was evident the property had not been inspected or properly cleaned following the previous tenants. We were forced to demand a basic standard of cleanliness before it was addressed.

Customer service throughout was appalling—dismissive, unresponsive, and entirely lacking in accountability. The cumulative effect of these failures caused significant and ongoing stress and anxiety.

This level of mismanagement is unacceptable. Avoid at all costs.

When we moved in to our flat, we were met with blood stained mattresses and mouldy walls that you would’ve expect to be clean when you move in - this was not the case when renting from Lexadon, and we have been left in the dark by the maintenance team, or expected to pay for replacing faulty equipment ourselves.

I would avoid renting from Lexadon - once they have your money, they don’t care for your wellbeing and give no thought to your health and safety.

AVOID. Late reports, a data breach, and a refund they never paid.

I booked Electrical (EICR), Fire Risk Assessment and EPC certificates with London Safety Certificate for my rental property in East London. Six weeks of chaos followed, and I'm still cleaning up their mess.

What happened:
- Reports promised in 24 hours took 6 weeks to arrive. I had to call them weekly to chase, then daily. They only do anything when you push hard.
- The reports weren't safe to use. They were marked as Passed but flagged "observations" that were serious enough they shouldn't have passed at all.
- They leaked another customer's personal data to me. One of the reports I received still had a previous client's personal information in it — they'd reused an old file and forgotten to clean it. I still have the document. I've reported this to the ICO as an unauthorised disclosure under UK GDPR.
- Every "fix" broke something else. Each new version introduced fresh errors or undid the previous corrections. It went on for weeks.
- The Lead eventually admitted on a call that they'd sent the wrong clerk and that one of the reports couldn't even be completed. He agreed to refund me. But that refund, agreed two months ago, has never arrived.

I kept everything: emails, WhatsApp messages, and call recordings. So I have every promise and every missed deadline.

I complained to ICO about the data breach, and last week met with Citizens Advice to report to the electrical certification body
Trading Standards too.

If you're a London landlord thinking about using them: their certificates aren't reliable, and if anything goes wrong at your property because of a bad report, that's your problem, not theirs.
The EIRC service was poor and I would not use them again.

I am extremely disappointed with the lack of support I have received from Hoveton & Wroxham Medical Practice during what has been a very difficult period for my mental health.

Following advice from my GP earlier this year, my Sertraline dosage was increased after a traumatic separation and significant personal stress. Recently, after experiencing common side effects from the medication, I stopped taking it and have since experienced worsening anxiety and depression symptoms.

I contacted the surgery urgently for help and was initially offered a same-day appointment, which was then cancelled. Since then, despite repeatedly explaining that this is a mental health and antidepressant withdrawal issue, I have continually been offered appointments weeks away in June.

I was advised yesterday that if I completed an online request, someone would contact me today to arrange support — nobody did. After chasing again today, I was once more offered a June appointment.

This is now the third time I have raised concerns about access to urgent care, and the situation itself is causing significant additional anxiety and distress. I run two businesses, care for a child with ASD, and reached out because I genuinely needed help.

I appreciate the pressures NHS staff are under, and the receptionist I spoke to yesterday was kind and helpful, but the system itself has completely failed me at a time when I most needed support.

Mental health concerns and antidepressant withdrawal should not be treated as routine matters that can simply wait weeks for review.

Update- reported this practice to the CQC as a doctor cancelled my medication without a review and without telling me!!! So have been throwing up with migraines for the last few days, Thankyou for that!!!!

WARNING!  If you are a Tenant, Properly will try to unjustly deduct from your deposit when you leave.

Properly (especially Michael, the Director), does not understand a fundamental concept in UK Tenancy Rights: The deposit rightfully belongs to the Tenant and if the Letting Agent wants to withdraw from this pool, the burden of proof is on them to provide evidence that damages were introduced by the Tenant.

To do this, they MUST clearly provide side-by-side evidence… something I asked for but they refused to provide. As such, we escalated to the TDS, who ruled overwhelmingly in my favour.

They tried to clawback £262.50 initially…and ultimately were only given £37.50 (£30.00 of which I agreed with before dispute)
This illustrates their incompetence and poor understanding of their domain.

To make matters worse, Michael misled the TDS adjudicator claiming: “The tenant was not happy to agree unless we removed all the items bar one and would not negotiate at all.” - This is a completely false. I kept asking for evidence but Michael didn’t want to get into “this kind of in-depth time-consuming discussion”.

This displays a lack of integrity on Michael’s part, who has only reinforced society’s stereotypes of Letting Agents.

Negative review regarding the behaviour of a Premier Fruits truck driver

I would like to report highly dangerous and unacceptable behaviour from a driver of a Premier Fruits truck that I witnessed while driving.

I was travelling with passengers (a total of 8 people, including family members, on our way to the airport). I was driving at approximately 39 miles per hour on a road with a 40 mph speed limit, fully within the legal speed limit. My vehicle is equipped with a continuous driving recording system that also monitors and records speed data, which will serve as evidence in the case being reported to the police.

Despite this, the truck driver began to aggressively tailgate my vehicle and flashed high beam lights in an intimidating and pressuring manner.

This behaviour created a real and serious road safety risk. There were children in the car who became visibly distressed and started crying due to the situation. In my opinion, this was a clear and serious violation of safe driving standards by a professional driver who should be held to the highest level of responsibility on the road.

It also raises a serious question about the driver’s awareness of potential consequences: does he fully understand what could have happened if another vehicle had suddenly cut in front of me, forcing an emergency stop? In such a scenario, his aggressive tailgating could have easily led to a serious collision involving multiple people and potentially life-threatening consequences.

The incident has been reported to the appropriate authorities, and the recorded footage, including speed data, will be available as supporting evidence.

I strongly believe that such behaviour is completely unacceptable and should not occur among professional drivers operating heavy goods vehicles, where the responsibility for the safety of others is especially significant.

If it were possible to give zero stars, we would.

I do not normally leave reviews, but after the experience we have had dealing with this firm, I felt it was important to share it.

Our experience dealing with this firm in relation to the administration of an estate has been extremely poor. The estate administration has now been ongoing for approximately four years, during which time communication and transparency have been consistently lacking.

As beneficiaries named in the Will, we did not instruct this firm ourselves, but unfortunately have had to deal with them throughout the administration process. More recently, after attempting to obtain clarity regarding the status of the estate, we experienced repeated delays, unanswered emails, and direct questions being ignored.

Even when updates were eventually provided, they still failed to address many of the reasonable questions we had raised regarding the administration of the estate, which only added to the ongoing frustration and lack of clarity surrounding the matter.

On multiple occasions we were told that further updates would be issued “shortly” or within a specified timeframe, only for those deadlines to repeatedly pass without explanation or apology. Most recently, we were informed that a further update had already been prepared and was simply awaiting approval. Weeks later, nothing has still been sent and further correspondence has again gone unanswered.

What has been most frustrating is not simply the delay itself, but the complete lack of accountability and transparency throughout the process. Even after formally raising concerns and requesting details of the firm’s complaints procedure, we still received no substantive response.

We fully appreciate that estate matters can sometimes be complex. However, there is no excuse for beneficiaries to be left with so little information for such a prolonged period of time while communication remains this poor and inconsistent.

At this stage we have entirely lost confidence in the firm’s handling of the matter and would strongly encourage others to carefully consider all available options before dealing with or instructing this firm in relation to estate administration matters.

If only you could give zero stars… the worst landlords we have dealt with in London.

We had an extremely disappointing experience with The Bedford Estates and would strongly caution anyone considering renting through them.

At the end of our tenancy, they attempted to deduct nearly £3,000 from our deposit for what can only be described as routine wear and tear after a two-year tenancy. This included full redecoration of multiple rooms, minor scuffs, ageing silicone, and trivial items such as removable tape, none of which reasonably justify the level of charges being proposed.

What was particularly concerning was that these deductions were issued before the check-out report was even provided. When the report was eventually shared, it actually contradicted many of the claims, categorising the majority of items as fair wear and tear or minor issues.

We also agreed to use their nominated cleaners (at their quoted price) to avoid any disputes at check-out, yet they still attempted to raise further cleaning-related issues afterwards. This felt both unreasonable and inconsistent.

In addition, they refused to provide even a basic factual reference for our onward tenancy, citing the service of a Section 21 notice (which is a no-fault eviction). This was both unhelpful and, frankly, demonstrated a lack of understanding of standard practice.

Separately, our personal details were shared with third-party marketing agents before we were formally notified in writing, which raised concerns around how our data was handled.

Throughout the process, communication was slow, unhelpful, and at times dismissive. The overall handling gave the impression of an attempt to pass refurbishment costs onto tenants rather than applying a fair and proportionate assessment.

For context, we have rented in London for over 10 years and have always had our deposits returned without issue. This experience was by far the worst we have encountered.

We are now forced to go through the deposit adjudication process to recover what should have been returned in the first place.

Proceed with caution. In fact, run the other way.
